question: Which economist took the subject of economics away from approaches that focus exclusively on income, growth and utility, with an increased emphasis on individual entitlements, capabilities, freedoms and rights?
solution:
The correct option is __**Amartya sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** About Amartya Sen.**

 
 
• He was awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory.
 
• He focuses exclusively on income, growth and utility, with an increased emphasis on individual entitlements, capabilities, freedoms and rights
 
• Some important books were written by him are:
 
 
• ​**Collective Choice and Social Welfare (1970)**
 
• **Poverty and Famines: An Essay on Entitlement and Deprivation (1981)**
 
• **Poverty and Famines: An Essay on Entitlement and Deprivation (1981)**
 
• **Rationality and Freedom (2002)**
 
• **The Argumentative Indian (2005)**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 PERSON
 PHILOSOPHY
 
 
 
 

 Robert Lucas
 
 
Robert Lucas won the Nobel prize for economics in 1995 for his rational-expectations theory.

 
That was based on decision-makers' abilities to predict the results of governmental economic policies and thus potentially subverts the intended effects of the policies

 
 
 

 
 Milton Friedman
 
 
 
American economist and educator, one of the leading proponents of monetarism in the second half of the 20th century.

 
He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Economics in 1976.

 
 
 

 Adam Smith
 
 
He is considered the father of modern economics.

 
Smith is most famous for his 1776 book, "The Wealth of Nations."
